provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Int family batch. Instagram-first, affluent buyers who decide fast; copy splits organising sessions and listing staging for agents. Staging copy never promises a faster or higher sale. No product or container brands. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Pantries, kitchens, closets, garages, playrooms and home offices, half-day and full-day sessions, how many sessions a room usually takes, and the separate product budget
pageStructurePlus.why: Organising clients buy by the room that's driving them mad. A page per room with a session count turns a scroll into a booked first visit.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Vacant and occupied staging, consult-only walkthroughs, furniture and decor rental periods, photo-day prep, de-staging after the sale, and how agents book
pageStructurePlus.why: Agents choose a stager on speed, inventory and how the rooms photograph. A clear staging page is what gets them to book the next listing.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Pre-move purges, packing plans, unpack-and-settle days in the new house, senior downsizing with family, and donation and consignment drop-offs
pageStructurePlus.why: Moves are the moment people pay for organising. A page built around the move date catches buyers who never thought they'd hire an organiser.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Bins, baskets, drawer dividers and shelf risers, custom labels, who shops and how products are billed, and returning what isn't used
pageStructurePlus.why: Clients worry about surprise product costs. Explaining the product budget up front makes the session price easy to say yes to.

pageStructurePlus.contains: What happens at the first visit, a judgement-free approach, confidentiality, what to keep or let go, and how donation runs work
pageStructurePlus.why: Embarrassment is the main reason people don't book. A calm first-session page removes it and gets the inquiry sent.

designDirections.name: Fresh Start
designDirections.bestFor: Solo professional organisers booking pantry and closet sessions from an inquiry form
designDirections.headlineSample: Professional home organizing in {City}, room by room
designDirections.whyItFits: Peach and soft rounded type feel kind and unjudging, which is what an embarrassed first-time client needs, and the page leads to a short inquiry.

designDirections.name: Before and Beautiful
designDirections.bestFor: Organisers and stagers with strong before-and-after pantries, closets and staged rooms to show
designDirections.headlineSample: Organized homes and staged listings across {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo, Terracotta Kiln, fails the CTA contrast rule. Rosewood keeps the warm, design-aware feel with an accent that passes, and its Didone display suits lifestyle before-and-afters.

designDirections.name: Listing Ready
designDirections.bestFor: Stagers working luxury listings and organisers serving high-end homes who sell on taste
designDirections.headlineSample: Home staging for {City} listings that photograph beautifully
designDirections.whyItFits: Gallery white with a Didone display steps aside so staged rooms look like a magazine spread, the way agents want to present a listing.

openers.line: Searched professional organizers in {City} and found your listing with lovely reviews, but no website. Someone embarrassed about their pantry wants to read how a first session works before reaching out.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what an organizing client would land on: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your organizing work lives entirely on Instagram and it's gorgeous. But nobody searching 'home organizer {City}' lands on your grid, and DMs are a hard place to book a session.
openers.hook: Check the bio link and listing. If both lead to Instagram or nothing, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Your organizing grid with booking built in: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your bio link opens a page of buttons, and none of them explain sessions, product costs or staging. That's where a ready-to-book client gives up.
openers.hook: Tap their bio link and note what's there. If it's a list of buttons with no service detail, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A proper organizing and staging page behind your bio link: {demo-link}

openers.line: On my phone your site's before-and-after pantry photos load one at a time and the inquiry button is hidden. Your organizing clients find you on their phones.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your organizing before-and-afters, built for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Booking an organizer means DMing a stranger about your messiest room. A short form asking which room and when would feel far less awkward.
openers.hook: Check for any form or booking. If inquiries only happen through DMs, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A gentle organizing inquiry form, room by room: {demo-link}

openers.line: You stage listings too, but it's mixed in with pantries on the grid. Agents looking for a home stager need their own page with inventory and booking.
openers.hook: Look for staging posts on their grid. If any, name one.
openers.linkLine: A home staging page built for agents: {demo-link}

openers.line: Reviewers say you made them feel zero judgement and their home finally works. That's the exact fear new organizing clients have, and it lives only on Maps.
openers.hook: Copy one review phrase about judgement, calm or the result. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews next to the organized rooms: {demo-link}

openers.line: January is when everyone books a home organizer. The organizers who appear in that search in December fill the first quarter.
openers.hook: Use this November to January. Mention the new year in the reply.
openers.linkLine: Ready for the new-year organizing rush: {demo-link}

openers.line: Spring is listing season, and agents need stagers booked before photo day. A staging page they can book from at night wins those listings.
openers.hook: Use this February to April. Mention spring listings in the reply.
openers.linkLine: A staging booking page ready for spring listings: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're looking for organizing assistants. Good ones want to see the kind of homes and standards they'd be working with before applying.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: An organizing site with a page for new team members: {demo-link}

openers.line: You organize homes across {City}, but someone in {Neighborhood} can't tell if you'll come to them. That neighbourhood plus 'home organizer' is what they search.
openers.hook: Find neighbourhoods named in posts or reviews. Use the most affluent.
openers.linkLine: An organizing page for each area you cover: {demo-link}

openers.line: Moves and downsizing are when people finally hire help. A page built around unpacking and senior moves would catch clients who never followed an organizer.
openers.hook: Look for any move or unpack post. If they do moves, lead with this.
openers.linkLine: A moving and downsizing page for your organizing business: {demo-link}

openers.line: Letting someone go through your closets is personal. A page about your first session, privacy and judgement-free approach makes that first message easier to send.
openers.hook: Check whether they ever describe the first session. If not, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Your first organizing session explained, privacy first: {demo-link}

openers.line: Looks like agents tag you on staged listings. When an agent recommends you to a seller, the seller looks you up before saying yes to staging.
openers.hook: Find an agent tag on their staging posts. Name them if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Where an agent's staging referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is the kind of organized room people save and send to their partner. It should be the first thing a new client sees.
openers.hook: Pick their newest before-and-after and name the room.
openers.linkLine: That organized room, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted is so satisfying to look at.

I was looking for home organizers in {City} and found {Business Name} on Instagram, but no site where someone can read how a first session works or where agents can book staging. I put together a sample site, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would you like to see it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case this got lost in your DMs. Here's the sample organizing and staging site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has sessions by room, a gentle inquiry form, a first-session and privacy page, and a separate staging page for agents. If it's not for you, just say so.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for home organizers and stagers here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did you see it?"

IF NO:
"No worries. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with organizing sessions by room, a gentle inquiry form and a staging page for agents, plus marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I text you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many room and staging pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a business your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, roughly a couple of whole-home sessions."
"Which is growing faster for you, organizing or staging? We'd lead with that."

CLOSE:
"I'll send a short scope and the deposit invoice, and we'll pull your favourite before-and-afters off Instagram together."

objections.objection: Instagram brings me all my clients.
objections.handler: "It brings followers. Clients searching 'professional organizer {City}' on Google never see your grid. The site catches them and sends them back to it."
"Then the site lets you choose: whole-home and staging work over single drawers, and an inquiry form that tells you the room before you reply."

objections.objection: Agents just text me for staging.
objections.handler: "New agents don't have your number yet. A staging page with your inventory and booking is how they find you between referrals."

objections.objection: I don't want to post prices.
objections.handler: "We don't need to. We can show 'sessions from' or leave it to the consult call. Most clients just want to know how sessions and products work."
"You don't have to be. Inquiries arrive as a text or email, and any change is a message to me."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}: sessions by room, an inquiry form, a first-session page and a staging page."

email.subject: Organizing and staging site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for home organizers and stagers in {City} and made a sample one for {Business Name}. I'll text you the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm taking the {Business Name} organizing demo down on Friday.

Want it kept? One word is plenty.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, the new-year organizing rush is coming and spring listings won't be far behind. Thought of you.

The site is still ready, same price. {demo-link} for another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a couple of whole-home organizing sessions, never to an hourly rate.
Organizing and staging are two buyers. Quote the staging page set as its own line if they do both.
The inquiry form is the core: room, size of the problem, timeline and a photo option. Keep it short and kind.
Price the before-and-after gallery by the number of rooms pulled from Instagram and captioned.
Staging inventory pages only make sense for stagers who own furniture. Consult-only stagers need a simpler page.
Launch by November so it's found before the January organizing rush.

lineItems.description: Max when the page has several before-and-afters, a session-count guide and a product notes section.

lineItems.item: Gentle inquiry form with room and photo
lineItems.description: Max with photo upload, a move-date field, a staging-or-organizing switch and booking for a call.
Max with vacant and occupied staging pages, an inventory gallery and an agent booking form.
Max when many posts are sorted into rooms, paired before-and-after and captioned.
Max with separate unpack, purge and senior downsizing sections and a move-date checklist.
Max when each page has its own organized rooms and a local review.

whatElseYouSell.name: Styled before-and-after organizing shoot
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Matched angles before and after, with the labels readable and the light soft. One shoot makes a pantry reveal look the way it felt."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, booked for the 'before' of their next big room.

whatElseYouSell.name: Instagram and Pinterest organizing content plan
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Reels of drawers being sorted already travel. A steady plan with a booking link turns that reach into organizing sessions."

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile organizing posts
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A new organized room or staged listing on your Google profile each week, so 'home organizer near me' shows you working."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review request after the reveal
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The evening after the organizing reveal, the client gets a text asking for a review while they keep opening the pantry to look."

whatElseYouSell.name: Agent staging lookbook
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short digital lookbook of staged rooms and your inventory for agents, so they can picture their listing staged before calling."

whatElseYouSell.name: New-year organizing campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Resolutions about clutter peak right after the holidays. Ads and posts that run that week fill your January organizing calendar before other pros do."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in October, run in late December.

whatElseYouSell.name: Gift card and gift session page
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "An organizing session makes a great gift for new parents and movers. A gift page sells sessions in December and May."

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The agents who book your staging need listing sites and a vendor page, and your staged rooms are their best photos."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Agents buy marketing constantly and already trust the stager.

withoutAI.whoPays: The closet company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "When a client needs a real closet system, you refer an installer. That installer needs a site, and their clients need an organizer."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Constant two-way referral between sorting and building.

withoutAI.whoPays: The mover, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Movers see every downsizer and every unpack. The mover you work with needs a site, and their clients need an organizer."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Moves trigger organizing; movers hear first.

withoutAI.whoPays: The photographer, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The photographer who shoots your staged listings needs a portfolio site, and your rooms are the best shots in it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Stagers and photographers work every listing together.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Downsizing clients need an estate sale company for what doesn't move. That company needs a site, and they send organizing work back."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Downsizing involves both, and estate sale companies rarely have good sites.

withoutAI.whoPays: The cleaning company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Cleaners see cluttered homes every week. The cleaning company you trust needs a site, and their clients need a home organizer."

withAI.pitchLine: "Agents upload walkthrough photos and get a draft declutter and staging checklist for the seller, with the stager to book."
withAI.whyItWorks: Agents write that list for every listing; the tool routes staging to your client.

withAI.pitchLine: "The organizer's notes on what's stored become a draft closet design brief, so the installer quotes faster."
withAI.whyItWorks: Both trades save time and the referral sticks.

withAI.pitchLine: "Families enter the new home's room sizes and get a draft of which furniture fits, with organizing help to book."
withAI.whyItWorks: Downsizing decisions are the slowest part of senior moves.

withAI.route: Photographer's shot list from staging notes
withAI.pitchLine: "The stager's room notes become a draft shot list for the photographer, so photo day runs on time."
withAI.whyItWorks: Both get faster listings; agents notice.

withAI.pitchLine: "Photos of sale items go in, draft descriptions and category tags come out for the estate sale listing."
withAI.whyItWorks: Writing listings is their slowest task.

withAI.route: Cleaning company's add-on organizing offer bot
withAI.pitchLine: "When a cleaning client mentions clutter, the bot offers an organizing session and books it with your client."
withAI.whyItWorks: Cleaners earn goodwill and the organizer gets warm clients.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for organizing inquiries
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Mid-session with a client? Missed callers get a kind text asking which room needs organizing and whether it's for a move or a listing."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and two lines of wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Discovery call booking with room questions
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Clients pick a free discovery call slot and answer three gentle questions about the room, so the organizing call starts informed."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 1. Needs their calendar and questions.

softwareAI.name: Review replies that name the organized room
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A thrilled review about a new playroom gets a warm reply drafted in your voice, ready for one tap."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs ten past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Session deposit and product reimbursement invoicing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Session deposits at booking and organizing product receipts billed after, each sent automatically with a card link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their deposit rule and product billing policy.

softwareAI.name: Room-photo organizing plan draft
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The client uploads photos of the pantry or closet and it drafts a session estimate and a product list for you to adjust."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs past rooms with session counts and products used. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Staging inventory catalogue
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every sofa, rug and lamp in the staging warehouse tagged with photos and where it's deployed, so you know what's free for the next listing."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, for stagers who own inventory. Needs a photo pass of the warehouse.

softwareAI.name: Agent staging request assistant
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Agents message at night with an address and photo day; it asks vacant or occupied, room count and style, and holds a staging date."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their calendar and staging intake questions. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Client home map with labels and locations
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each organized home gets a simple map of what lives where, shared with the family, so the system survives after you leave."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their label system and a habit of logging rooms at the end of a session.

softwareAI.name: Staging schedule and de-stage tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every staged listing with install date, photo day, rental period and de-stage date on one board, so inventory never gets stuck."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, for stagers. Needs their rental terms and current listings.

softwareAI.name: Staging layout suggester from listing photos
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Upload photos of an empty living room and it drafts a staging layout from your own inventory catalogue."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, after the inventory catalogue. Needs past staged rooms. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Maintenance refresh reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Three months after a big organizing project, the client gets a friendly refresh-session offer. Repeat bookings from happy homes."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs past clients with dates.

softwareAI.name: Client page with plan, products and dates
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Clients see the organizing plan, approve the product list and see session dates, without a long text thread."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their plan template.

softwareAI.name: Chatbot on sessions, products and privacy
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'do I need to clean before you come' and 'who buys the bins' at midnight, from your own organizing rules."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their FAQ and availability. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Donation run scheduler
softwareAI.pitchLine: "At the end of each organizing session, donation pickups or drop-offs get booked and the client gets a receipt reminder."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their donation partners and process.

softwareAI.name: Revenue by service type
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See whether pantries, moves or staging actually pay best per hour once product shopping and drive time are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a season of sessions with hours.

softwareAI.name: Room guide writer from captions
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Your Instagram captions become a new organizing guide each month, like 'a pantry for a family of five', approved before it's live."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs caption access and approval. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Product list builder with links
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Build a client's organizing product list from your favourites, with quantities and sizes, ready to share or shop."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their go-to products and sizes.

softwareAI.name: Voice notes to session summary
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Talk through what was done and what's next on the drive home, and it drafts the client's organizing session summary."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their summary template. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Gift session sales page and voucher codes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Sell organizing gift sessions online with a code the recipient redeems when booking."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, before December or Mother's Day.

softwareAI.name: Assistant applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Organizing assistant applicants answer questions on discretion, lifting and weekend availability, so you call only real fits."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Any time they post a hiring note. Needs must-haves and pay. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the organizing inquiry and plan tools
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every solo organizer books through DMs. The inquiry form and plan draft I built for one organizer works for any of them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Many solo operators with the same workflow; cheap monthly tools spread.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The professional organizers' association, per bundle
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Give member organizers a site template with room pages and a gentle inquiry form as a benefit of joining."
"A brokerage-wide staging request page with approved stagers by area, so every agent books staging the same way."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Brokerages want consistent listings and an easy vendor list.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Stagers across a metro list idle inventory for rent to each other, so a sofa doesn't sit in storage while a listing waits."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Idle furniture is money tied up; a shared catalogue fixes it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies get organizer clients who can't afford custom builds. License my organizing template with room pages ready."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Low-ticket clients only pay off on a template.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Senior communities help new residents downsize. A move-in services page with vetted organizers makes it smoother."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Communities fill units faster when moves are easy.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Relocating employees get an unpack-and-settle day. A booking page with vetted organizers per city covers it."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Relocation firms buy services at scale.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Container and closet retailer's organizer finder
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Shoppers buying bins ask who could set it all up. An organizer finder on the store's site answers."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Retailers sell more when the product gets used well.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "New organizers need session pricing sheets, a first-session script and a simple site. Sell the pack your first client uses."
"Staging training programs need a site that fills classes. Your stager client's rooms show students the standard."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Training has budgets tied to enrolment.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: An organizing client in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Staging and organizing don't travel across metros, so after {City} the same gentle-inquiry site can go to an Instagram-only pro in the next one."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse everything.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Organizers stuck on a page of buttons
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Organizers living on a bio-link page of buttons get a real one-page site with room sessions and booking in a week."

upsellLadder.offer: Organizing site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "Organizing site and care plan on one contract, so a new before-and-after is a text to me."

upsellLadder.trigger: The first client booked through the site has their reveal.
upsellLadder.line: "That pantry client is thrilled. Let's ask every organizing client the evening of the reveal."

upsellLadder.trigger: They book a big room that will make a dramatic after.
upsellLadder.line: "Let's shoot that garage before you start. The organizing reveal will lead the site."

upsellLadder.trigger: An agent books staging through the site.
upsellLadder.line: "An agent found your staging page. A lookbook gets the rest of their office booking."

upsellLadder.trigger: Ninety days of inquiries with photos, and they're spending evenings estimating sessions.
upsellLadder.line: "You're estimating every organizing inquiry by hand at night. Let the plan draft do the first pass."

upsellLadder.trigger: They have several staged listings out at once.
upsellLadder.line: "Several staged homes at once means inventory gets lost. Let's put every listing on one staging board."

upsellLadder.trigger: Past clients mention things slipping a few months later.
upsellLadder.line: "Organized homes drift back to old habits. A refresh-session offer brings those clients back to you."
